title: Minimal Sufficient Circuits for Safety-Relevant Refusals: How Fragile Are They?

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong: understanding refusal circuit fragility directly informs adversarial robustness assessments. If refusals rely on a thin shared circuit, it reveals a single-point-of-failure safety architecture with clear deployment implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: automated circuit discovery on instruction-tuned models (Gemma-2-2B-IT) is supported by TransformerLens. Measuring node ablation effects on refusal rate is conceptually straightforward with established tools.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: identify refusal circuit on one category, measure ablation robustness, repeat for 2-3 categories, compare overlap. Clear deliverable (fragility assessment). Achievable in 30 hours with a small model.

novelty.reasoning: The single-direction refusal finding (Arditi et al.) established that refusal is concentrated and therefore fragile. Follow-up work on abliteration robustness (ReFAT, extended refusal fine-tuning) and cross-model transfer confirms this. However, the specific proposal to systematically map minimal sufficient circuits per harm category and measure cross-category overlap/fragility as a structured robustness assessment has not been fully executed. The fragility concern is known; the systematic category-by-category circuit comparison adds incremental novelty.

evidence.source: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction (NeurIPS 2024)
evidence.finding: Arditi et al. demonstrate that refusal is mediated by a one-dimensional subspace across 13 open-source chat models up to 72B, and a single direction can be intervened upon to bypass or induce refusal.
Introduces framework for transferring refusal interventions across architectures without target-side refusal supervision, confirming shared refusal circuit structure across models.

evidence.source: SafeSteer: Interpretable Safety Steering with Refusal-Evasion in LLMs (2025)
evidence.finding: Addresses safety steering in the context of refusal evasion, providing tools for understanding how refusal mechanisms can be circumvented.

evidence.source: Improving Alignment and Robustness with Circuit Breakers (2024)
evidence.finding: Proposes circuit breakers to improve robustness of safety mechanisms against adversarial attacks, acknowledging fragility of standard refusal mechanisms.
